metrics.justification: Fronted the contested 10-year licence renewal for the rare-earths processor Lynas (announced 2 Mar 2026) with stricter conditions (halting radioactive-residue production after five years, barring a new permanent disposal facility), and managed the political fallout; environmental groups say the existing stockpiled waste stays unresolved. Decisive action with measurable conditions, but contested (anchor 2).

citation.title: Lynas given 10-year licence extension, but with stricter conditions, says Chang

metrics.justification: Brought the Malaysian Space Board Act 2022 into full force (with the 2024 regulations, from 1 Jan 2025), standing up the Space Authority Division and the Malaysian Space Board as the sector regulator; the national nuclear-technology policy targets remain forward-dated. A gazetted, operative legal framework delivered alongside aspirational policy (anchor 3).

Convened the National Science Council (chaired by the Prime Minister, 4 Nov 2024) with a stated remit to coordinate science and technology across federal, state, academic and industry levels, and secured a raised national research allocation in Budget 2025. Coordinating intent and funding, but measurable institutional strengthening not yet documented (anchor 2).

metrics.justification: On the Lynas renewal he addressed the charge that the government had reversed its long-standing opposition, explaining the decision on the record as continuity ("not gone against our promise") with a 2031 waste-elimination goal, rather than ignoring the criticism. Candour on a contested shift, framed as continuity rather than a clean admission (anchor 2).
